mandatoryClauses.name: Landlord's Title
mandatoryClauses.description: Basis of landlord's ownership / right to evict — registered sale deed, allotment, succession etc.

mandatoryClauses.name: Statutory / Contractual Ground
mandatoryClauses.description: Specific ground — e.g., non-payment of rent for X months, subletting without consent, bona fide requirement, expiry of lease

filingChecklist: Confirm which Act governs the tenancy — state Rent Control Act vs Transfer of Property Act vs Model Tenancy Act (where notified)
Notice must align with the ending of a month of tenancy for monthly tenancies under TPA 106
Minimum 15 days notice for monthly tenancy (TPA S.106 as amended in 2002 — earlier was 15 days for premises let for manufacturing, 30 days for others); confirm post-amendment position
Minimum 6 months notice for tenancy from year to year (TPA S.106)
Where state Rent Act applies, follow that Act's notice format and grounds — many require eviction only on specified statutory grounds
Notice sent by Registered Post AD / Speed Post AD
Postal receipts and AD card preserved
Copy of lease deed / rent receipts annexed
Title documents preserved for production in suit
Limitation: Eviction suit under TPA = 12 years for possession (Article 65); Rent recovery = 3 years (Article 52)

validation_rules.description: Applicable State Rent Act must be identified before drafting; default to TPA S.106 only for non-rent-controlled premises
Monthly tenancy minimum 15 days notice, ending with month of tenancy (TPA 106 post-2002 amendment)
Most state Rent Acts permit eviction only on specified grounds — generic 'I want my premises back' is insufficient
For non-payment ground, give tenant statutory opportunity to pay arrears before eviction

promptInstructions: Draft a Legal Notice for Eviction / Notice to Quit.

FIRST determine the governing law — state Rent Control Act (where premises are within Act's coverage) OR Transfer of Property Act, 1882 Section 106 (for non-rent-controlled premises) OR Model Tenancy Act 2021 (where adopted).
Identify the state — Delhi / Maharashtra / Karnataka / Tamil Nadu / UP / Bihar / Jharkhand / West Bengal — and apply the corresponding Rent Act provisions.
Establish landlord's title and the tenancy particulars — premises description, tenancy start date, rent, rent period, purpose.
State the specific ground for eviction — non-payment, subletting, bona fide requirement, nuisance, structural damage, expiry of lease.
Where ground is non-payment, particularise arrears (period + amount) and give a cure opportunity.
Compute the correct notice period: monthly tenancy = minimum 15 days ending with month of tenancy (TPA S.106 post-2002); annual tenancy = 6 months; state Rent Act may prescribe different period.
Demand vacant possession by a specific date.
Claim arrears and mesne profits for the period of unauthorised occupation.
State the competent forum — civil court for TPA suit, or Rent Controller / specified forum under state Rent Act.
Terminate the tenancy expressly with effect from the date of expiry of notice.
Use firm but professional legal language.
Do NOT generate the advocate signature block — it is added programmatically.
